role: independent reading and typography methods reviewer
method: Single model visual examination; no human participant research. Blind pair examined before actual-font proof; no blind key or other reports read.

tests.name: blind pair examination
tests.result: Completed visual inspection of every A/B pair at supplied resolution.

tests.name: actual font render and examination
tests.renderer: Pillow FreeType, variable font axes set explicitly
tests.conditions: 14/16/18px weight400 opsz14; Russian/English short paragraphs and UI labels; confusion strings; 48px weight500 opsz48 Russian/English headings; 38px weight400 opsz38 confusion string
tests.result: Completed visual examination; body rhythm and heading spacing coherent in these samples.

blind_assessment.reason: No reliable visible difference in word spacing, line length, texture, or individual forms in the supplied phrases. This is not proof of font equivalence.
Both pairs show similarly steady spacing and intact counters; no visible change that justifies a preference.

blind_assessment.confidence: high for visible I cue; low for measured reading benefit
blind_assessment.reason: B adds clear horizontal terminals to capital I, differentiating it from lowercase l. Other shown forms offer no convincing A/B preference. O/0 remain similar oval silhouettes.

ui.reason: Ordinary 14–18px labels are coherent in the actual render. Dense ambiguous identifiers need task testing; capital I terminals help but lowercase l and numeral1 remain narrow, and O/0 differentiation is modest.

headings.reason: Visual pass limited to 48px weight500 opsz48 Russian and English samples: even rhythm, no conspicuous collisions or counter loss.

body.reason: Three-line Russian/English samples at 14–18px are visually legible and balanced. Paragraphs are too short to establish reading performance; no browser/device proof included.

sustained_reading.reason: No human reading speed, comprehension, fatigue, or longer-session data were collected.

findings.concrete_condition: Blind 54px weight100/900 I l 1 sequences; actual 14–18px sequences
findings.evidence: B capital I has crossbars; actual-font capital I also visibly has them. Narrow l and1 still require attention at the smallest size. No measured confusion rate.
findings.recommendation: Retain the capital-I cue; test identifier transcription before making further glyph changes.
findings.acceptance_test: Randomized 6–8-character identifiers containing I/l/1 at14/16/18px; compare target to a chosen incumbent font, count character substitutions and completion time.

findings.concrete_condition: Actual-font O/0 and Cyrillic З/3 in context-free 14–18px strings
findings.evidence: O/0 depend mainly on subtle proportions; З/3 have closely related silhouettes. The 38px row makes proportions easier to inspect but does not resolve small-size performance.
findings.recommendation: Test numeric/letter contexts and consider an optional distinct-zero feature only if task errors justify it; do not infer failure from silhouette similarity alone.
findings.acceptance_test: Counterbalanced code and account-number transcription tasks; inspect pair-specific confusion counts and compare with incumbent. No claim of improved distinction without observed error reduction.

findings.concrete_condition: 14/16/18px weight400 opsz14 paragraphs, 48px weight500 opsz48 headings
findings.evidence: Actual proof shows consistent word boundaries, intact counters, and no conspicuous local spacing defects across the sampled phrases.
findings.recommendation: Keep current spacing pending broader text and device checks; no visual basis here for global tracking changes.
findings.acceptance_test: Render varied Russian/English paragraphs in target browsers at1x/2x, 14–18px, normal UI line heights and400–600 weights; no clipping, overlaps, or word-boundary ambiguity in review.

human_pilot.participants: 8–12 target readers, with fluent Russian and English represented; exploratory pilot, not statistical validation.
human_pilot.design: Within-person, counterbalanced current-font versus incumbent-font order, masked labels; rotate matched passages so a participant never rereads the same passage. Match rendered x-height and line length for the principal reading comparison, then separately test native product CSS settings.
human_pilot.tasks: Two matched 500–700-word passages per font with comprehension questions, one10-minute reading block per font plus discomfort rating, and24 randomized short identifier-transcription trials per font at14/16/18px.
human_pilot.record: Reading time, comprehension correctness, character-specific transcription errors, time per identifier, and subjective comfort after each block. Record device/DPR, language fluency, corrective lenses, and text-size preference.
human_pilot.decision: Use paired participant results to identify recurring confusions and adverse reading signals. Treat any repeatable confusion cluster or comprehension reduction as a follow-up trigger; do not declare equivalence or sustained-reading superiority from this small pilot. Predefine the acceptable margin for a larger confirmatory study.

limitations: Visual judgement by one model; not a human readability study.
No prior reports, blind key, or source generation code inspected. Actual-font proof may permit inference about one glyph but no A/B identity was requested or revealed.
Pillow rendering is not a browser/OS font-rasterization audit.
Only selected sizes, axes, text, white background, and short paragraphs examined; no italic, multilingual coverage, or accessibility compliance determination.
Supplied blind image inspected visually; no pixel difference measurement.
